ground_truth: The description is wrong, the laser is on and was triggered by the solar panel
response:
There are two common reasons in this setup — and the picture shows the likely one:

- The laser is being powered through the solar-panel/outlet chain, but the flashlight in front of the solar panel is not turned on, so the panel isn’t producing electricity and the laser won’t fire. (The flashlight must be bumped/pressed to turn it on so it lights the solar panel.)

Other things to check if that’s not it:
- Make sure the laser is plugged into a real ELECTRICAL_OUTLET (one that has juice) and not into a LASER-ACTIVATED PLUG (those only power things when they themselves are hit by the correct color laser).
- Some parts also have their own on/off switch — click the laser/plug to toggle it.

Quick fix: bump the flashlight (or drop something on its button) so the solar panel gets light — the outlet will power the laser and it will turn on.

ground_truth: The ball constantly falls on the spring board and triggers it. As soon the blimp reaches it the spring board triggers a diagonal fly
response:
Because when the puzzle starts the blimp is intersecting/touching the arch. The game’s physics immediately resolves that overlap by pushing the blimp out along the contact normal, so its initial movement vector is diagonal instead of perfectly horizontal. 

Fixes: move the blimp slightly clear of the arch (or place it on a flat surface) so it isn’t touching at start; then it will fly in the straight horizontal line you expect.

ground_truth: The switch of the fan is not turned on
response:
Because the outlet you plugged the fan into isn’t providing power. In IM2 there are different outlet types — some are always-on (the electrical outlet), but the small square you have is the switch/outlet, which must be turned on (or pressed) or a laser/solar source must supply power to a laser-activated plug.

How to fix:
- If it’s an Electric Switch & Outlet (the little box with a switch), drop something on the switch or bump it to flip it on.
- Or plug the fan into an always-on Electrical Outlet instead.
- If you used a Laser-Activated Plug, make sure a laser of the correct color is hitting the plug and the laser is powered.
- If you used a Solar Panel, shine a light on the panel (flashlight, lava lamp, etc.).
- Also check you actually placed the Electric Fan (not a vacuum or motor) and that it isn’t flipped so the airflow is reversed in a way you don’t notice.

One of those will get the fan blowing.
